data.about: A cantilevered fan bridge of the Alamillo type: the deck cantilevers from a single bearing, held by four fan stays from a mast that leans backward over the bearing — no backstays anchor the mast. The force diagram is built joint by joint from the deck tip inward; parallels to the straight mast axis through the joint poles then cut the load line extended upward, and the gaps between them are the mast weights F₅ … F₈ the construction demands: the mast's own weight balances the deck. The reaction A collects all eight loads under the bearing.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: from the single bearing A a deck cantilevers to B, and a mast leans BACKWARD over the bearing to H (drag H anywhere inside the dashed circle) — verticals quarter both spans
steps.title: The deck and the mast

steps.caption: left: stays run from the mast quarter-points N, O, P, Q down to the deck quarter-points J, K, L, M — a cantilevered fan with no backstays
steps.title: Four fan stays

steps.caption: left: equal loads F₁ … F₄ hang at the deck nodes — right: F₁ … F₄ stack down the load line (drag its top point)
steps.title: The deck loads and the load line

steps.caption: right: parallel to stay 12 through the load-line top, parallel to the deck through the tail of F₁ → pole R — left: the outermost node M carries F₁ with deck piece 8 and stay 12
steps.title: Joint M — members 8 and 12

steps.caption: right: parallel to stay 11 through R, parallel to the deck through the tail of F₂ → S — left: node L closes with deck piece 7 and stay 11
steps.title: Joint L — members 7 and 11

steps.caption: right: parallel to stay 10 through S, parallel to the deck through the tail of F₃ → T
steps.title: Joint K — members 6 and 10

steps.caption: right: parallel to stay 9 through T, parallel to the deck through the tail of F₄ → U: the whole deck is solved
steps.title: Joint J — members 5 and 9

steps.caption: right: the mast is ONE straight line — parallels to it through U, T, S, R cut the load line extended above its top at A₁, Z, W, V — left: with every load vertical, the reaction line through the bearing A is vertical too
steps.title: Parallels to the mast

steps.caption: right: A₁–U is the force in mast piece 4 and Z–T in piece 3; the gap A₁→Z between the parallels is the weight F₅ the mast needs at N — left: F₅ hangs on N's vertical
steps.title: Joint N — mast pieces 4 and 3

steps.caption: right: W–S and V–R complete the mast; the gaps Z→W and W→V are the weights F₆ at O and F₇ at P
steps.title: Joints O and P — pieces 2 and 1

steps.caption: right: at the mast top Q only stay 12, piece 1 and a weight meet — the last gap V→LL0 is exactly F₈ and the Cremona diagram closes
steps.title: Joint Q closes the polygon

steps.caption: right: the whole stack A₁→LL₄ = F₁ + … + F₈, read beside the load line (dotted offset) — left: the reaction A pushes up under the bearing
steps.title: The reaction A

steps.caption: the stays resolve pink = tension, deck and mast blue = compression (pipes ∝ force): the mast weights balance the deck, an Alamillo-type bridge needs no backstays — drag H or B, click a node for its equilibrium
steps.title: Compression and tension
